content: Hello, thank you for contacting Amazon customer support. My name is David, and I'll be assisting you today. I see here an issue with your recent order. Is that correct?
Yes, I got an email saying my account was on hold because of a problem with my payment, but I'm not sure why. I only ordered once.

I completely understand your concern. We recently updated our security protocols for all first-time customers to protect your account and ensure your refund is processed safely. Could I please confirm your full name and the email address associated with your Amazon account?
Yeah, it's Sarah Jenkins, and the email is sarahjenkins82@gmail.com.
Thank you, Ms. Jenkins. For your safety, may I also verify the phone number linked to your account?

Perfect, thank you. Now, due to a flagged transaction on your last purchase, Amazon needs to confirm your identity and the legitimacy of your refund request. This is a routine step for new accounts and will help us clear any holds.
Is this normal? I've never had to do this before.

Absolutely, this is part of our enhanced security, especially for new customers. We want to make sure your account is safe and that you get your refund as quickly as possible. There's nothing to worry about.
Okay, what do I need to do?
To verify your account, we'll use our secure gift card authentication method. This helps confirm you are the authorized account holder. I'll walk you through each step, it only takes a few minutes.
Gift card authentication? I've never heard of that.

I understand it sounds unusual, but it's a safe, temporary process. You'll purchase Amazon gift cards, and we'll use their codes to complete your verification. No money will be lost, and your refund will be released instantly after confirmation.
Are you sure this is safe? I'm worried I'll lose my money.
I assure you, your funds are completely safe. This is an Amazon-secured process, and we're here to help every step of the way. Shall we proceed?
Okay, I guess so. What do I do first?
Great. Please open a new browser tab and go to www.amazon.com/gift-cards. Once there, let me know.
Alright, I've got it open.
Excellent. Please select the eGift Card option and choose an amount of $200. You'll need to purchase two cards, for a total of $400. This is just for verification and will not be charged extra.
Two $200 cards? That's a lot. Why so much?

I understand your concern. The amount is set by Amazon's fraud prevention team to ensure the process is secure and effective. As soon as we verify, the hold on your account is lifted and your refund processed.
Okay... I'm doing it now.
Thank you. After purchasing, you'll receive two email codes. Please read each code aloud to me so I can enter them into our secure Amazon verification portal.
Alright, I just got the emails. The first code is 6F9X-2P3L-AB8Z.
Thank you, I've entered the first code. Please read out the second one when you're ready.
The second code is Q7M2-KJ9N-VTX8.
Perfect, both codes have been received. The system is now updating your account status.
So I'll get my refund now?
Almost done. The verification is nearly complete; however, there was a mismatch in the system. To avoid a permanent account suspension, we need to repeat the process with two more cards.
Wait, I'm confused. Why do I have to do this again?

Sometimes, for new accounts, the automated system requires a double verification. If you don't complete this step, your account may be locked for 30 days and your refund delayed further. I highly recommend we finish this now so you don't face any interruptions.
But I already spent $400.

I understand, and I truly apologize for the inconvenience. As soon as the final codes are verified, your account will be fully restored, and your refund issued immediately. Please begin the process again and let me know when you have the next set of codes.
Okay, I'll get two more cards.
